provenance.head: 97e09d9a0c4d64e4a8ae1f0d5c2b1dc7d2c19d86
provenance.reviewers: 4 read-only Sonnet subagents (correctness, security, ticket-fit, tests) on the RR briefs

findings.title: Angular HttpParams leaves '+' unencoded, so it is read as a space
findings.observation: Searching "A+B" would send a literal '+', which Spring decodes as a space.
findings.why: Refuted: this spec asserts '+' goes out as %2B, and it passes on Angular 16.

findings.title: Owner deleted between the page and graph queries yields a 500
findings.observation: A concurrent delete between the queries throws IllegalStateException. The 500 body echoes the owner id, and the total can disagree with the rows.
findings.why: openspec/changes/paginate-sort-owners/design.md:44 mandates surfacing it; cross-request snapshot is out of scope (design.md:92).

findings.title: Deep page numbers allow costly OFFSET scans
findings.observation: page up to ~107M is accepted, and each call runs a COUNT plus a deep OFFSET.
findings.why: Numbered offset paging chosen (design.md:62); OWNER_ADMIN-only endpoint; load tests deferred.

findings.title: lastName has no length bound
findings.observation: Several KB of prefix goes unchecked into the LIKE and count queries.
findings.why: Same as before this change; Tomcat's request-size limits cap it; bound literal, no injection.

findings.title: Issue #25 comment and Bizu notification not done
findings.observation: Task 4.4 is unticked, so #25 still carries the stale "implemented" claim and nobody was told about the breaking rollout.
findings.why: The human forbade posting anything on GitHub in this run; left open in tasks.md.

findings.title: Name sorts by last name although the cell shows "First Last"
findings.observation: "Zed Adams" sorts before "Alice Baker" even though the cell starts with the first name.
findings.why: The human decided this in Q&A.md:30 (Q3).

findings.title: Performance at 100k owners unverified
findings.observation: The latency test was only compiled; the indexes and the 3-SELECT bound were checked only on small fixtures.
findings.why: Deferred for budget by the proposal (proposal.md:89, design.md:60).

findings.title: First/last paginator buttons and a global validation handler were not asked for
findings.observation: The global HandlerMethodValidationException handler changes 400 bodies for other endpoints, and the first/last buttons were not requested.
findings.why: Buttons are in proposal.md:69; no other endpoint has parameter constraints, these were 500s before.

findings.title: Expected order computed by Java comparators, not DB collation
findings.observation: Mixed-case or accented names would sort differently under en_US collation, and the ASCII-only fixtures cannot reveal that.
findings.why: The fixtures are same-case ASCII on purpose, so both orders agree; collation is not under test.

findings.title: Migration test checks index definitions, not query plans
findings.observation: The planner may not use the indexes for the LIKE or ORDER BY, and the test would still pass.
findings.why: The planner ignores indexes on tiny tables; EXPLAIN on 100k rows is deferred (design.md:60).

autofixes.title: Line over 119 chars blocked the push
autofixes.observation: The commit-time formatter wrapped the sort parameter's inline message onto a 122-char line, and check-line-length.py refused the push.
autofixes.fix: Moved the message into a SORT_MESSAGE constant.

autofixes.title: Add-visit fixtures searched only the first page of owners
autofixes.observation: Both helpers looked for an owner with a pet among the first 10 owners only. A seed where those 10 have no pets fails the scenario, even though such owners exist on later pages.
autofixes.fix: Page through the list until an owner with a pet turns up, or the pages run out.

autofixes.title: A failed load dropped the user's place with no retry
autofixes.observation: After a 5xx the table and paginator disappear. The only way back was a new search, which resets to page 0. The user's page, size and sort were never re-requested.
autofixes.fix: The error banner gets a "Try again" button that re-sends the failed page's exact query.

autofixes.title: Query budget not pinned for default size or City sort
autofixes.observation: The ≤3-SELECT test ran only sizes 5 and 20, always sorted by Name, so an N+1 on the default size or the City sort would stay green.
autofixes.fix: Parameterized over size and sort: 5 name,asc / 10 city,desc / 20 name,desc.

assumptions.title: "Unrepresentable" page means its offset overflows Hibernate's int
assumptions.alternative: Accept any int page and let a huge offset fail at query time
assumptions.why: The spec (specs/owner-list/spec.md:23) demands a 400 for unrepresentable pages without defining the term. Capping at MAX_INT/20 is the tightest bound that holds at every allowed size, but a lower business cap would be equally defensible.

assumptions.title: Invalid parameters rejected by bean validation plus a @OneOf constraint
assumptions.alternative: A custom exception that rest throws and rest.error maps
assumptions.why: packages.puml forbids rest → rest.error, so a custom exception would need an architecture change. Spring's own HandlerMethodValidationException keeps both packages independent; the cost is one small constraint annotation.

assumptions.title: Type-mismatch 400 applies to every REST endpoint, not only the list
assumptions.alternative: Scope the 400 to listOwners and keep 500 elsewhere
assumptions.why: The spec needs page=abc to return 400, and a 500 for malformed input is wrong everywhere. Still, /api/owners/abc changing from 500 to 400 is a contract change nobody asked for.

assumptions.title: Allowed sizes and the sort default stated in OpenAPI descriptions
assumptions.alternative: A custom OpenAPI customizer emitting an integer enum and default
assumptions.why: springdoc renders allowableValues as strings, which Spectral rejects, and drops a default that contains a comma. Prose keeps the lint green, but machines cannot read the 5/10/20 rule from the schema.

assumptions.title: A failure hides the grid instead of keeping stale rows
assumptions.alternative: Keep the last rows visible under the error banner
assumptions.why: The spec says a failure must not look like a result, and stale rows under a new query would. Showing the previous rows greyed out is a reasonable UX that the spec does not exclude.

assumptions.title: An empty page within a non-empty result shows a "go back" row
assumptions.alternative: Jump to the last valid page automatically
assumptions.why: The spec only forbids claiming "no matches" and requires navigation to stay available. Auto-jumping would send an extra request nobody triggered.
